tool_input.prompt:
Small hardening on `~/Coding/punt-labs/ethos`, branch `fix/module-path-v4`, `Makefile` `tools:` target.

**Context — the reported bug is NOT real, but we're changing the code anyway.** Bugbot filed a high-severity finding claiming the `\`-continued `#` comments you added inside the recipe cause the shell to comment out the remainder of the joined command, so checksum matching, verification, extract, and install never run and `make tools` exits 0 silently.

I tested it and it's false. GNU Make passes the backslash-newlines through to the shell rather than collapsing them, and POSIX specifies that a `#` comment discards characters up to *but excluding* the newline — so the trailing backslash is consumed as comment text and the newline still terminates the comment. Verified with a structural repro under `/bin/sh`, `/bin/dash`, and `/bin/bash`: a variable set before the comment block is intact after it, and every subsequent statement executes. Your own fixture run corroborates it — `...tar.gz: OK` and a successful install are both downstream of that comment block, so the recipe plainly reaches them.

**Why change it regardless.** This construct has now tripped two careful readers in a row: you initially (you removed the `\`s, which really does break it, by splitting the recipe into separate shell invocations and discarding variable state) and then an automated reviewer (which added them back conceptually and reached the opposite wrong conclusion). A correct-but-treacherous construct in the middle of a security-relevant verification step is a liability — the next person to touch it has a coin flip's chance of "fixing" it into an actual break, in either direction.

**The change:** move that explanatory comment block out of the recipe body and above the `tools:` target as ordinary Make comments (plain `#` lines at column 0, no `\` continuations, no `$$` escaping needed). Keep every word of the explanation — it's good and it's load-bearing for the next reader. The recipe body should then contain only executable statements with their `\` continuations.

While you're there, check whether any other recipe in this Makefile has `\`-continued `#` comments inside the body, and give them the same treatment.

Verify by running the real recipe end-to-end again with your stubbed-`curl` adversarial fixture — confirm it still matches exactly one line, verifies, extracts, and installs, and that the tamper/zero-match/duplicate-match cases still fail correctly. Do not regress the awk field-equality matcher from `f9ab726`.

Run `make check`. Commit. Do not push — return to me.

out=""
url=""
prev=""
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$prev" = "-o" ]; then
    out="$arg"
  fi
  prev="$arg"
done
# last argument is the URL
eval url="\${$#}"
name=$(basename "$url")
src="$FIXTURE_DIR/$name"
if [ ! -f "$src" ]; then
  echo "stub curl: no fixture for $name" >&2
  exit 22
fi
cp "$src" "$out"
